note: Researcher's manual review of the 30 sampled candidates in samename.json (criteria.md), in sample order. a = RISC-V suspected to have the same problem; b = no; c = cannot tell.

rows.label: b

rows.label: b
rows.reason: RISC-V checks irqs_pending, which includes interrupts injected by a userspace irqchip

rows.label: b
rows.reason: arm64 left [_text,_stext) unmapped; RISC-V maps the whole kernel image contiguously

rows.label: b
rows.reason: x86 cpa_lock rule; RISC-V has no such lock

rows.label: c
rows.reason: invalid large leaf mappings: RISC-V splits before changing and its pmd_present counts the R/W/X bits, so PMD-level invalid leaves stay leaves; PUD level not checked, no caller found that invalidates an aligned 1GB range

rows.label: b
rows.reason: tail-call hierarchy needs subprog tail calls; the RV32 JIT does not declare bpf_jit_supports_subprog_tailcalls

rows.label: b
rows.reason: RISC-V uses the generic compat ftruncate64 (__ARCH_WANT_COMPAT_FTRUNCATE64), fixed in fs/open.c by the same commit; the same name is a macro

rows.label: b
rows.reason: RISC-V already uses memcpy for file mode and copy_from_user otherwise

rows.label: a
rows.reason: memory hotplug: arch_add_memory -> create_linear_mapping_range (void) -> late page-table allocators that BUG_ON on failure; arm64 now returns -ENOMEM. M8 (lagging behind the reference architecture's evolution)

rows.label: b
rows.reason: RISC-V counts slots as round_up(arg_size, 8) / 8, so a 16-byte argument takes two
